Your sequences have somehow become out of sync. If I had to guess this could be because the sequences are not in the same schema as the rest of Gitea.

There have been multiple recent issues (closed) on this issue - can you look at those for how to figure out how to update them.

It would be helpful to know if you're running Gitea in a schema in order to help us figure out how this happened. Or if you used a backup and restore method, or something else

I can add existing topics but not new ones.

Dude, I don't know if you mean to be quite as rude as you're appearing - I'm sorry that there was a mistake and an error but we can't get right all the time and I'm only inferring from what you're saying as to what the problem could be.

I do all my work on Gitea for free. I get no payment despite the many hours of time I put in to this project. It appears I get even less thanks - a little bit of appreciation for the fact that you're getting help for free would go a long way.

I'm sorry something has gone wrong and I'm just trying to help. I appreciate how stressful things, especially databases, can be when they're not working.

--- 

In terms of the Topic table, it should have a sequence attached to its primary key:

```sql
SELECT * FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name = 'topic';
```

for me reveals that the column default for the `id` column is `nextval('topic_id_seq'::regclass)`

Now `pg_dump -st topic testgitea` for me gives: (dropping the comments and any data)

```
CREATE TABLE gtestschema.topic (
    id bigint NOT NULL,
    name character varying(50),
    repo_count integer,
    created_unix bigint,
    updated_unix bigint
);

ALTER TABLE gtestschema.topic OWNER TO gitea;

CREATE SEQUENCE gtestschema.topic_id_seq
    START WITH 1
    INCREMENT BY 1
    NO MINVALUE
    NO MAXVALUE
    CACHE 1;

ALTER TABLE gtestschema.topic_id_seq OWNER TO gitea;
ALTER SEQUENCE gtestschema.topic_id_seq OWNED BY gtestschema.topic.id;

ALTER TABLE ONLY gtestschema.topic ALTER COLUMN id SET DEFAULT nextval('gtestschema.topic_id_seq'::regclass);

ALTER TABLE ONLY gtestschema.topic
    ADD CONSTRAINT topic_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id);

CREATE INDEX "IDX_topic_created_unix" ON gtestschema.topic USING btree (created_unix);

CREATE INDEX "IDX_topic_updated_unix" ON gtestschema.topic USING btree (updated_unix);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "UQE_topic_name" ON gtestschema.topic USING btree (name);
```

Where `gtestschema` is the schema the topic table is in.

How do we explain this `tmp_recreate__topic_id_seq`?

The `tmp_recreate__topic_id_seq` will be related to a migration which is supposed to fix the problem of a missing Primary key on the topic table - which clearly  isn't working properly on postgres - (likely because we haven't accounted for the sequences in PostgreSQL). The sequence should have been attached to the Primary Key ID on the copied temporary topic table, and was expected to have increased in turn when copying the data into the table, finally when the topic table was renamed should have continued to be attached. Without more information I can only guess that the issue is when the data was copied in to the temporary table the sequence isn't updated and when the table is renamed the sequence isn't renamed too. 

Assuming that you discover that the `tmp_recreate__topic_id_seq` is attached to the `id` column of the `topic` table then:
`SELECT setval('tmp_recreate__topic_id_seq', (SELECT MAX(id) FROM topic));` should restore the correct value and  `ALTER SEQUENCE tmp_recreate__topic_id_seq RENAME TO topic_id_seq` should restore things completely to normal.

---

Now that I think I understand the problem I can adjust the recreate-table commands and functions to properly account for this newly discovered complexity in postgres - however it would be helpful to just confirm that this is what is going on first.

Unfortunately you didn't tell what the values of the sequences was before or after your restore. Restore shouldn't have been completely necessary as even if the sequences were all zero'd all you would have needed to do was set the sequences back to their values using setval. It would have been helpful to know if the sequences were completely missing after recreate-table or just incorrect.

```sql
SELECT last_value FROM tmp_recreate__topic_id_seq;
```

and similarly for a few chosen other sequences e.g. `user_id_seq` would have been useful. However I should be able to figure this out with testing myself.

> Dude, I don't know if you mean to be quite as rude as you're appearing - I'm sorry that there was a mistake and an error but we can't get right all the time and I'm only inferring from what you're saying as to what the problem could be.

I don't want to discuss off-topic things here that are not related with the problem so please keep the issue and related topics as a priority. However bellow I clarify some things.

> R: That's great

It's no rudeness but bewilderment because you are suggesting me execute stuff in my database as well as run the gitea tool to see what happen (that's fine) but then you tell me something like _"your sequences are out of kilter, you need to fix them and We don't have a command to do that for you because we didn't expect this to be such a problem"_.
Sure but It would be better to just say that you can not simply help because lack of feedback from my side so then I could provide you the necessary to find the root of the problem.

No, I'm not taking the rude approach here I just want to solve the problem that until now isn't yet since as far as I know there are other users facing similar issues.
Therefore please don't take my comments personal or any kind of. 

> I do all my work on Gitea for free. I get no payment despite the many hours of time I put in to this project. It appears I get even less thanks - a little bit of appreciation for the fact that you're getting help for free would go a long way.

Sure, I understand since I do too OSS in my free time (or even with extra hours) without profit of any kind even with no economic retribution for the effort, but It's not a complaint or something like that, I'm fine with it. However I receive contributions and feedback which are what I appreciate more.
Therefore I appreciate your effort here too, no doubts.

> I'm sorry something has gone wrong and I'm just trying to help. I appreciate how stressful things, especially databases, can be when they're not working.

It's part of our job sometimes face annoyance or difficulties but let's work together to solve the problem.

---

For now I'm replaying this until get my workstation again in next hours then I will answer the technical questions needed as well as providing more insights in order to help to solve the problem.

issue.body:
Unfortunately there is a subtle problem with recreatetable on postgres which
leads to the sequences not being renamed and  being left at 0.

Fix #14725

Signed-off-by: Andrew Thornton <art27@cantab.net>

body:
Sorry for the delay below my reply.

> Assuming that you discover that the `tmp_recreate__topic_id_seq` is attached to the `id` column of the `topic` table then:

Yes, `tmp_recreate__topic_id_seq` is attached to column's `id` of `topic` I have just confirmed:

```sql
SELECT table_catalog, table_schema, column_name, table_name, column_default
FROM information_schema.columns
WHERE table_name = 'topic' AND column_name = 'id';

-- table_catalog|table_schema|column_name|table_name|column_default                                 |
-- -------------|------------|-----------|----------|-----------------------------------------------|
-- gitea        |public      |id         |topic     |nextval('tmp_recreate__topic_id_seq'::regclass)|
```

> `SELECT setval('tmp_recreate__topic_id_seq', (SELECT MAX(id) FROM topic));` should restore the correct value and `ALTER SEQUENCE tmp_recreate__topic_id_seq RENAME TO topic_id_seq` should restore things completely to normal.

It seems working again, the rename was successfully. But as you said probably was because a failed migration process that left topic table and sequences in an inconsistent state. Anyway here the SQL dump of `topic` table before the ALTER SEQUENCE:

<details>
  <summary>public.topic</summary>

```sh
pg_dump -U gitea -st topic gitea
```

